alice: quick sanity check — i'm seeing blank User-Agent in our request logs for a subset of go-sdk traffic. is the UA supposed to be set by the client or by our proxy? :eyes:
ben: the SDK sets a default UA by concatenating sdk-name/version + runtime, e.g. "redwood-go/0.7.2 go/1.20". if it's blank it usually means something upstream stripped it (nginx/proxy) or the client was constructed with UA override.
alice: ah ok. any recommended way to force a UA from the app side? need to surface app name for debugging.
ben: you can pass a header in the client config. e.g. in go: `client := redwood.NewClient(opts.WithHeader("User-Agent", "myapp/checkout-service/1.2.3"))` — that will be preserved unless the proxy removes it.
carol: note: some infra rules sanitize UA for privacy, but we shouldn't strip custom UAs for internal envs. filing infra ticket if you can repro with a curl sample.
alice: repro attached: `curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY\" \"https://api.rw.example/v1/generate\"` — UA shows up. only happens from go-sdk.
ben: that points to the client layer. can you paste the minimal client init? maybe a race or header reuse bug.
alice: pasted: ```go
cfg := redwood.Config{APIKey: os.Getenv("RW_KEY")}
client := redwood.New(cfg)
// request code uses streaming with retries
```
ben: thanks. streaming + retry path historically reuses lower-level http.Request and we had a bug where UA header was cleared on reconnect. i pushed a small fix to preserve headers across request clones. i'll link PR.
dev-bot: deploy queued for redwood/go-sdk@fix/preserve-ua (build #3289) :rocket:
carol: while we're on headers — tracing propagation question: does the SDK propagate W3C traceparent by default or use our custom `x-rw-trace` header?
ben: SDK will propagate existing traceparent/traceparent headers from incoming context (w3c). for internal tracing we add `x-rw-trace` as a convenience header for legacy systems, but it should not override an existing traceparent. if you're instrumenting, attach the trace context to the request context and SDK will forward the trace headers.
alice: if a retry happens, does the trace id stay the same? we want all attempts correlated to one span.
ben: yes — we preserve the trace id across retries when the retry is client-side and not an explicit new operation. the fix also ensures trace headers are copied when cloning the request for backoff.
carol: one more — customers asking how to disable client metrics (we log counters to our telemetry backend). any simple opt-out?
ben: env var `REDWOOD_SDK_TELEMETRY=0` disables emitting metrics+usage from the client. also per-client opt-out: `redwood.New(cfg.WithTelemetry(false))` for languages that expose it. examples: JS: `new Redwood({ apiKey, telemetry: false })` Python: `Client(api_key, telemetry=False)`
alice: perfect. can we add that to the FAQ and a short snippet in the go docs?
ben: yes i'll add a tiny section and a public note about env var precedence.
carol: re: streaming quirks — someone reported partial events on reconnect leaving the client in `open` state. any mitigation?
ben: workaround today is to set smaller chunk window and enable keepalive. long-term we have a fix to handle reconnect-and-resume semantics, tracking last acked token. i'll put a note in the SDK release notes.
alice: thanks all — i'll wait for the PR and infra ticket. :thumbsup:
ben: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/412 — includes UA + trace header preservation and a unit test for retry clone. please smoke test.
carol: infra ticket created #INF-2234 to check proxy UA passthrough for internal routes.
alice: tested the branch locally — UA shows up and trace header maintained on retries. marking resolved on my side.
dev-bot: alice added :heavy_check_mark: reaction
alice: closing out, will open followups if customer sees anything. thanks!
